parties:
Mizanur Rahman and others ------ Petitioners
vs
Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) 
and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: The petitioners are the employees of the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) serving as Office Assistant-cum-Stenographers, Welders, Assistant Accounts Officers etc. at various places of the country. The employees of the BADC are "public servants" within the meaning of section 2(d) of the Public Servants (Retirement) Act, 1974. Section 4 read with section 9 of the said Act creates a vested right in favor of all public servants including the employees of the BADC that they will not be forcibly retired from service prior to completion of twenty-five years of service. However, as part of the policy of the Government to reform the public sector, there were in-depth discussions among the relevant and concerned quarters over the past decades for streamlining the BADC by reducing the number of its employees. Such discussions, motivated by the pressure of donor agencies, have been part of a general strategy for reform. Following extensive consultations with the relevant quarters including BADC Workers Union, as the representative of the BADC employees, a scheme of re-organization of the BADC was adopted by the Government in 1999 which was published in the Bangladesh Gazette vide notification No. Krishi-5/Mo-2/98 (Angsha-8)/727 dated 17-11-1999. It is apparent from. Clauses 3 and 5 of the said notification dated 17-11-1999 that the Government decided; firstly, that the member of the. employees of the BADC would be reduced to 6,800 of whom 1,700 and 5,100 would be officers and staffers respectively. Secondly, the workforce that was in excess of the said figure of 6800 would be progressively reduced by way of usual retirement and voluntary retirement. Further with a view to facilitate in the voluntary retirement of the BADC employees, a sum of Taka 160 crore would be allocated to the BADC by the Ministry of Finance. Anyway, the import  the notification dated 17-11-1999 was to preserve and uphold the provisions of the Public. Servants (Retirement) Act, 1974 and to protect the BADC employees against any forced retirement. On the basis of the notification dated 17-11-1999, a good number of the employees of the BADC participated in the Voluntary retirement scheme, popularly known as Golden Hand shake Scheme resulting in considerable reduction of the workforce of the BADC. But because of non-availability of sufficient funds at the disposal of the BADC, the notification dated 17-11-1999 could not be availed of fully resulting in dissatisfaction among the employees of the BADC. In this regard; Several correspondences were made to the concerned authority, which primarily focused on the availability of sufficient funds to make the Golden Handshake Scheme more attractive, but without any success. However in response to the BADC's letter dated 23-9-2002, the Government issued two memos dated 6-10-2002 and 7-10-2002 to the effect that the Government had decided to reduce excess manpower of the BADC through lump sum payment, though no  mention was Made of voluntarily participation in any such scheme of lump sum payment. Thereafter, all of a sudden and without prior consultation, the impugned notification bearing No. Krishi-5/M0-34/99/714 dated 26-10-2002 was made purporting to amend Classes 4 and 5 of the notification No. Krishi-5/Mo-2/98 (Angsha-8)/727 dated 17-11-1999. From the impugned notification dated 26-10-2002, it is obvious that Clauses 4 and 5' of the notification No. Krishi-5 /Mo-2/98(Angsha-8)/727 dated 17-11-1999 stand amended so that manpower in excess of 6800 will be terminated from. service through onetime lump sum payment without making any reference to voluntary participation of the employees in the said scheme. Since the scheme contemplated voluntary retirement prior to the purported amendment, the obvious presumption is that the respondents are intending to make compulsory retirement of the BADC employees even before completion of twenty-five years of service pursuant to the impugned notification dated 26-10-2002.
